prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Stronger for Scotland: the SNP offers a progressive alternative to Westminster austerity, promising to make Scotland’s voice louder and deliver fairer, greener, more prosperous politics across the UK. The party will never put the Tories into power; if there is an anti‑Tory majority, it will work with others to keep them out and press Labour to deliver real change.

Economic and fiscal plan
- End austerity with modest, responsible spending rises each year, prioritising investment in infrastructure, jobs, skills and productivity, while reducing deficit and debt as a share of income.
- Fairer taxation: restore the 50p top rate, tax bankers’ bonuses, increase the bank levy, introduce a mansion tax, abolish non‑dom status, curb avoidance, review pension tax relief for the wealthiest.
- Create a sovereign wealth fund; seed‑fund a Scottish Business Development Bank; improve export finance; support SMEs with prompt‑payment protections and higher Employment Allowance.
- Raise the minimum wage to £8.70 by 2020; promote the living wage; curb exploitative zero‑hours contracts.

Public services and living standards
- NHS: protect from privatisation and increase UK spending by £9.5bn real‑terms by 2020–21, delivering an extra £2bn for NHS Scotland.
- Childcare: expand free nursery education to 30 hours a week for all 3–4 year‑olds and eligible 2‑year‑olds.
- Housing: support a UK target of 100,000 affordable homes a year and expand building in Scotland.
- Energy bills: shift ECO to general taxation and compel suppliers to pass on wholesale price cuts, saving households around £100.

Fair welfare and pensions
- Scrap the Bedroom Tax; halt Universal Credit and PIP rollout; reverse DLA→PIP; raise work allowance by 20%; overhaul sanctions and Work Capability Assessments.
- Increase Carer’s Allowance to JSA level; uprate benefits by at least the cost of living.
- Protect pensioners with the triple lock; set the single‑tier pension at £160; review the rise to state pension age 67.

Jobs, sectors and regions
- Back city and northern investment, including HS2 built north–south and south–north and faster broadband/4G with a Universal Service Obligation.
- Support oil and gas jobs, deploy the Oil and Gas Authority in Aberdeen, expand the Green Investment Bank, and boost creative industries with a fairer BBC Scotland share (+£100m).

Defence, climate and environment
- Oppose Trident renewal and redirect savings to services; strengthen conventional capabilities and veteran support.
- Match Scotland’s climate ambition; back offshore, onshore, hydro and community energy; maintain a fracking moratorium; support species protection.

Democracy, rights and media
- Reform Westminster: introduce STV for Commons, abolish the House of Lords, extend the vote to 16–17 year‑olds, enable real MP recall.
- Protect the Human Rights Act and ECHR; oppose mass surveillance “snoopers’ charter.”
- Devolve broadcasting; secure a fair BBC settlement for Scotland; remove VAT on sanitary products; drive equal pay audits.

Europe and the world
- Keep Scotland in the EU; oppose withdrawal and require a UK‑wide “double majority” for any exit; secure devolved speaking rights in EU forums; exempt the NHS and Scottish Water from TTIP.
- Support a two‑state solution for Israel/Palestine; maintain 0.7% GNI for aid; appoint an LGBTI rights envoy.

Home Rule
- Implement Smith Commission in full, without UK vetoes, and go further to full fiscal responsibility; prioritise devolution of employment, welfare, taxation, national insurance and equality to build a fairer, more prosperous Scotland.
